TennisExplorer lists Betway/Interwetten at 1.65/2.10 and Ladbrokes at 1.65/2.15, implying roughly 56% without margin; OddsDigger independently shows 1.625/2.10. Their reported doubles ranks, #102/#95 versus #169/#133, favor the more experienced pair, although current official individual rankings could not be fully verified. Both teams are 6-0 in sets this week. Hidalgo/Kestelboim's opening opponents were weak, and their semifinal required two extended tiebreaks. Miguel/Ribeiro beat Arias/Carou convincingly and nearly defeated Kestelboim/Zormann in Curitiba; that different partnership is not team H2H. Common-opponent comparisons offer only weak Brazilian encouragement after accounting for partner changes. Ribeiro's Antofagasta title strengthens the counter-case. Guto played singles and doubles yesterday; one report describes left-foot treatment, but his subsequent 6-3 6-3 doubles win limits its significance. Zakharova's 6-1, 7-5 win over #44 Starodubtseva supplies the stronger immediate opponent-quality signal, while her repeated hard-court wins over Linda Fruhvirtova contrast with Kudermetova's August defeat. Those comparisons justify only a small adjustment. Kudermetova has the better last-five record, 3-2 versus 2-3, and her Tauson upset is meaningful; Ma and Shao were softer wins. Facing Andreeva or Bencic is not equivalent to beating them. Kudermetova's nine aces and 24/26 first-serve points won today limit conviction. The 2-1 H2H is stale, with its latest meeting favoring her. No verified current injury or workload asymmetry emerged. These are public results, not demonstrably unpriced information. Secondary schedules indicate Oct 18 at 03:00 UTC, but the official OOP could not be retrieved; start remains unverified.

edge_factors.detail: Bobichon beat Mannarino and Boulais at Rennes; four straight wins preceded a heavy quarterfinal loss to Schoolkate.

Coulibaly returned from over two months out at Rennes; that win receives less weight than his ranking alone suggests.
Durasovic has substantially more indoor experience and beat Sakellaridis at Lyon one day after Sakellaridis beat Bobichon.

rows.headline: Bobichon narrowly preferred, but the evidence does not justify buying at 53¢
rows.analysis: Fair probabilities: Bobichon 56%, Durasovic 44%. Bobichon (#566) has the better recent singles results and won their July meeting, but those signals are insufficient for a large advantage. His Rennes run included a genuine Mannarino upset and another Boulais win; Kobelt was a very soft opponent and Coulibaly was returning from a lengthy absence. Schoolkate then beat him decisively. Durasovic (#467, career-high #222) lost four of his last five singles matches, yet his established indoor record deserves more weight than his poor outdoor-hard season here. Older common-opponent chains conflict and add essentially nothing. Bobichon's four Rennes wins came against left-handers, limiting their direct relevance against right-handed Durasovic. No current injury or extreme-fatigue evidence warrants an adjustment; Durasovic played Davis Cup doubles on Sep 19. Bookmaker prices imply roughly 54-55% for Bobichon after removing margin. At 53¢, estimated fees and execution bring cost near 55.2¢: neither side offers credible value after uncertainty. Historical forecast feedback reinforces restraint without a mechanical probability deduction.

rows.title: Timofeeva vs Brantmeier
rows.tournament: Eupago Porto Open WTA 125 final, outdoor hard; Complexo Desportivo do Monte Aventino, Porto

edge_factors.detail: Timofeeva beat Knutson 6-1, 6-2 after Knutson's recent 11-3 stretch and two WTA 125 finals.
Timofeeva has two 2026 WTA 125 titles and a WTA 250 title; Brantmeier is contesting her first final at this level.
Brantmeier's 6-3, 6-0 win came against Kraus, described as exhausted after a 3:10 quarterfinal.
The NCAA singles champion only graduated this spring; her limited professional schedule weakens a literal #88 versus #385 comparison.
Brantmeier served 19 aces against Dodin earlier this month and has won all 12 singles sets in Porto.

rows.headline: Timofeeva has the stronger record, but 62¢ leaves no credible net edge
rows.analysis: Fair probabilities: Timofeeva 63%, Brantmeier 37%. Official WTA ranks are #88 and #385; the gap exaggerates their difference because Brantmeier recently left college. Timofeeva's dominant win over in-form Knutson, victory over rising Pohankova and established title record support favoritism. Brantmeier's six straight-set wins and serve are substantial counterevidence, although her best-ranked victim, Kraus, was explicitly reported exhausted. Shared-opponent chains provide almost no separation. Hard-court records favor Brantmeier numerically but involve unequal fields; neither current injury impact nor extreme fatigue is established. rows.headline: Yang/Zeng's proven partnership outweighs Aguiard's stronger singles credentials
rows.analysis: I favor Yang/Zeng at 68%. They have four titles together and a listed 22-16 career team record, versus no recorded Aguiard/Komagata partnership. Reported ATP doubles ranks are 438/590 versus 2463/unranked; direct ATP verification was blocked, so these are secondary-source values. Aguiard's 1-7 and Komagata's 0-2 professional doubles seasons support the experience gap, but partners and opposition matter. Yang's five consecutive doubles losses prevent stronger conviction. Their July title included lower-ranked opposition, and September's loss to Hsu/Zheng shows vulnerability. Aguiard's Challenger singles progress, weak favorable singles chains and Komagata's NJCAA doubles championship reduce my estimate below the bookmaker consensus. TennisExplorer lists Aguiard/Komagata versus Yang/Zeng at 3.23/1.34 with 1xBet and 3.00/1.30 with bwin, roughly 70–71% fair probability for Yang/Zeng; direct executable quotes were not confirmed. No current injury or exceptional fatigue adjustment is justified. The official OOP did not expose a verifiable start; live status remains unknown, with no positive evidence requiring a skip.

rows.title: Pokorny vs Zielinski

rows.headline: Pokorny's better clay wins narrowly outweigh Zielinski's stronger surface record
rows.analysis: Pokorny gets a cautious 57%. His Tulln qualifying wins over Ratti and Paulson were both upsets, and beating then-#197 Barrena 6-1, 6-4 on clay matters more than merely facing Challenger opposition. Zielinski lost his last three, including a clear defeat to Shylov as a 1.22 favorite; his latest wins were against much weaker opposition. However, Zielinski's clay record is substantial: 36-18 this season and 50-23 last year, versus Pokorny's 6-9 this season, including two league losses. Zielinski also beat Martineau and Boitan, so his success cannot be dismissed as soft draws. Current ranks #595 versus #581 barely separate them; Pokorny's #383 peak and broader Challenger exposure provide context, not certainty. Shared-opponent chains and style proxies add almost nothing. TennisExplorer lists bet365 at 1.57/2.25 and Unibet at 1.63/2.12, roughly 57-59% Pokorny after removing margin. No current injury or extreme fatigue is verified. The official OOP page exposes no schedule; third-party start times conflict and live status remains unverified. No medal.

rows.title: Khachanov vs Blockx
rows.tournament: US Open QF, outdoor hard (Flushing Meadows)
rows.headline: Blockx's rib is hurting his serve; Khachanov returns better than anyone he's beaten here
rows.analysis: Blockx is the better player in 2026 (live #26, Madrid SF over FAA/Cerundolo/Ruud, Estoril final) and has the two best wins of this fortnight: #5 seed Cobolli 6-7 6-3 6-0 6-3 and #24 Cerundolo in four. Khachanov is #50, went 16-18 pre-NY and lost to Tomic, Atmane and Kovacevic in July/August. But he's found his level here — bagel-adjacent wins over Burruchaga and Bonzi, an upset of FAA (who was ill), and a 3h50 five-set win over Tien showing he's physically fine with two days off. The feather is Blockx's rib: physio at 3-2 in set one vs Cerundolo, near-retirement, 'I still feel it' despite heavy medication, and it hurts specifically on serve — 17 aces/4 DFs vs Cobolli became 10 aces/7 DFs and 56% first serves vs Cerundolo. Khachanov returns better than either. Chains lean Blockx (Cobolli, Ruud), so this isn't clean, and bookmakers at 1.58 have already absorbed the injury. Lean Khachanov, no medal. Note: Wednesday's official order of play was not published at time of writing; feeds split between 15:30 and 18:30 UTC.

rows.analysis: Bookmakers have this 1.60/2.19 (~58% no-vig), matching Kalshi's 0.58 — so the whole case rests on the chains, and they are unusually clean. Chan/Joint beat Mertens/Shnaider at Cincinnati (7-6(4) 3-6 [10-3]); Hsieh/Ostapenko beat the same #14 seeds 6-4 6-4 on these very courts yesterday. Mihalikova/Nicholls beat Mertens/Shnaider in the Toronto QF; Hsieh/Ostapenko have beaten that pair twice in 2026, including at Cincinnati nine days later. Both chains are hard court, both inside four weeks, both corroborated on two pages. Underneath that, Hsieh/Ostapenko are a nine-month unit with two 2025 slam finals and a 2026 title; Mertens/Shnaider are a North-American-swing pairing playing their first slam together, away from their regular partners, 5-2 lifetime with two pre-USO losses. Fresher (2R walkover) and Mertens is the best doubles player on court, but chemistry and match reps sit with the seeds. I make it ~64%, a modest step above the price.

rows.headline: Rising 19yo with Monastir pedigree vs a rusty, drifting M15 journeyman
rows.analysis: Confirmed as M15 Monastir 1R, outdoor hard, 13:00 local (12:00 UTC) — Kalshi's 16:00 is a placeholder. Ranks favour Bertimon (#932 vs #1079) and that is what the Kalshi book is priced off, but the trend lines cross: Willwerth is 19, sitting at his career high, a 2025 AO junior finalist who has spent August in Challenger main draws (beat Chin 6-4 6-4 at Kingston 2, won the opening set off #172 Bueno, lost 4-6 6-2 4-6 to Mayo). rows.headline: Lajovic's clay 'specialism' is a 2019 label; his 2026 clay is 5-6 with losses to #180-200
rows.analysis: The price (Kalshi 0.57/0.58, books 1.66 vs 2.06) discounts a #65 to near coin-flip because clay is supposed to be the 36-year-old Serb's surface. It isn't anymore. Lajovic's 2026 clay ledger: 1R loss to Cecchinato at Montemar as the 8 seed, R16 loss to Roca Batalla (#~200) at Cattolica, R16 loss to Rocha at Perugia, RG qualifying 1R loss to Rodionov, Umag 1R loss to Van Assche. His only good 2026 stretch was on HARD (Lexington SF, beat Bonzi in Cincy qualy). He hasn't hit a clay ball in a match since June 12. Landaluce, by contrast, made a Rome QF on clay as a lucky loser beating Cilic, Bellucci and Medjedovic, took Medvedev to 7-5 in the third, and made RG R3 through two five-setters. He beat Lajovic 6-3 6-1 last October and beat Cecchinato on clay a fortnight after Lajovic lost to him. Add a wildcard-into-Davis-Cup-prep motivation edge and warm, quick Seville conditions that suit the 193cm hitter. The counter is genuine: Landaluce is streaky (April clay losses to Quinn and Collignon) and Lajovic still constructs points well on dirt. That caps this at bronze.

rows.headline: Sonego's current level is a tier higher; clay + H2H shrink the gap, don't close it
rows.analysis: Both are Italians back from ~3-month 2026 wrist layoffs and both flew home from a Sept 2 US Open five-setter, so travel/fatigue cancels. What separates them is present level. Sonego (#89) since Wimbledon has beaten Mannarino and Shang, made W-S R16 and pushed top-seed Zverev 4h53 on Ashe, with Zverev saying he'd have beaten most players. Passaro (#207, post-wrist) has been ordinary on clay since June: losses to Roca Batalla (6-0 set), Dalla Valle, Squire and, in his last clay match, 6-4 6-1 to Kicker at Todi. His good week was hard-court US Open qualifying. The counter-case is real and is why this is 60c not 75c: Passaro won the only clay meeting 6-3 6-2 (Turin CH SF 2024) when Sonego had just beaten Coria and Wolf, Sonego is 1-5 on clay in 2025 and 2-6 in 2026, and a 6:30pm coastal night start makes heavy, slow balls that suit a grinder over a flat net-rusher. Moroni is a full-time ITF pro, #922 with a Nov-2025 career high of #470, three ITF singles titles, ex-Wake Forest, and 69-34 lifetime on hard (44-15 in 2025) - and Pozzuoli is fast cement. De Giorgio is a 27-year-old Neapolitan club player: unranked, career high #1442, EUR4,000 in career prize money, 62-61 lifetime with 53-54 of it on clay, and just two pro matches in 2026, both this week in his home qualifying draw. He has qualified here in 2024 and 2025 and been beaten 0-6 1-6 and 5-7 1-6 in the main draw. Bookmakers have Moroni 1.15 / De Giorgio 4.50. The honest counter-case is Moroni's 2026: 3-8, a Dec-Mar layoff and a July retirement that cost him six more weeks, plus three weeks off since a straight-sets loss to #1161 Juszczak. That is why this is 0.80, not 0.90. But form slumps do not close a 1,200-place gap on a surface that suits the better player.

rows.headline: Osorio's Quito results narrow the gap enough to favor his 42¢ contract
rows.analysis: I estimate 46% versus the supplied 42¢ ask. Hernandez remains the likelier winner, but Osorio offers the better price. [PokerStars](https://www.pokerstars.es/en/sports/tennis/2/matches/) quotes 1.53/2.30, implying 40% Osorio after removing margin; TennisExplorer quotes 1.56/2.22 at 1xBet, about 41%. My modest upward adjustment reflects Osorio's straight-set win over McCormick, who beat Hernandez here last week, and six sets played this week versus Hernandez's eight. Both are 4-1 over their last five, but Hernandez's wins came against weaker opposition. Osorio's Bini loss and Hernandez's stronger career and opposing Oliveira chain limit the adjustment. The old UTR result receives negligible weight. No medal: these form signals are public and bookmakers have already shortened Osorio. Reported ATP ranks are #484/#680, corroborated across results providers and federation reporting; direct ATP pages were inaccessible. The [official OOP](https://www.itftennis.com/en/tournament/m15-quito/ecu/2026/m-itf-ecu-2026-008/order-of-play/) exposed no schedule, so start is null; secondary feeds suggest Oct 17 around 17:30 UTC but disagree.

River Bet lists Basile 2.20/Gschwendtner 1.56, equivalent to 58.5% Gschwendtner after removing margin. [Odds](https://riverbet.ro/eveniment/15716/). Sep 21 ranking reproductions show #1464/#983; current official ATP confirmation was unavailable, and older pages disagree. Both operate mainly at Futures level. Basile finished college this spring, so his sparse ATP record understates his match experience. His two Telavi qualifying wins, particularly 6-2 6-3 today, remove grounds for penalising August's retirement as an active injury. His clay percentages are better, though boosted by qualifying opposition. Gschwendtner's Buzau semifinal included a retirement win and a soft Radu win; Monzon was the substantive scalp. Older shared-opponent comparisons favour him, but a recent chain through Freire Da Silva and Balducci counters them. No demonstrated fatigue or current injury advantage. Official OOP/start and live status remain unverified; no positive evidence requires skipping. Thin evidence merits no medal.

Petrofsky's upset of #1676 Galus is the stronger recent win by opponent ranking and materially restrains confidence. Both beat Doskocil on different surfaces; the longer Da Silva–Januchowski chain is too fragile to move the estimate meaningfully. Bet365's reported 1.57/2.25 implies 58.9% Zgola after removing margin; fetched River Bet odds of 1.56/2.20 broadly agree. No sharp-book quote was verified. However, Barrientos just won Sevilla, both opponents previously beat Donski on clay, and Barrientos beat Pieczonka there too. Common-opponent chains consequently add little overall. Neither exact partnership has a verified completed-match record, so individual success cannot establish team chemistry. TennisExplorer lists bet-at-home at 1.95/1.78 and 1xBet at 2.00/1.73, about 52-54% no-vig for the pick; another opened odds page remains 1.83/1.83. No reliable liquid sharp-book line was obtained. rows.title: Khachanov vs Blockx
rows.tournament: US Open QF, outdoor hard (Flushing Meadows)
rows.headline: Blockx's rib is hurting his serve; Khachanov returns better than anyone he's beaten here
rows.analysis: Blockx is the better player in 2026 (live #26, Madrid SF over FAA/Cerundolo/Ruud, Estoril final) and has the two best wins of this fortnight: #5 seed Cobolli 6-7 6-3 6-0 6-3 and #24 Cerundolo in four. Khachanov is #50, went 16-18 pre-NY and lost to Tomic, Atmane and Kovacevic in July/August. But he's found his level here — bagel-adjacent wins over Burruchaga and Bonzi, an upset of FAA (who was ill), and a 3h50 five-set win over Tien showing he's physically fine with two days off. The feather is Blockx's rib: physio at 3-2 in set one vs Cerundolo, near-retirement, 'I still feel it' despite heavy medication, and it hurts specifically on serve — 17 aces/4 DFs vs Cobolli became 10 aces/7 DFs and 56% first serves vs Cerundolo. Khachanov returns better than either. Chains lean Blockx (Cobolli, Ruud), so this isn't clean, and bookmakers at 1.58 have already absorbed the injury. Lean Khachanov, no medal. Note: Wednesday's official order of play was not published at time of writing; feeds split between 15:30 and 18:30 UTC.

rows.tournament: US Open 2026 women's doubles quarterfinal, outdoor hard, New York
rows.headline: Settled #4 pair with two live hard-court chains over a 5-week scratch pairing
rows.analysis: Bookmakers have this 1.60/2.19 (~58% no-vig), matching Kalshi's 0.58 — so the whole case rests on the chains, and they are unusually clean. Chan/Joint beat Mertens/Shnaider at Cincinnati (7-6(4) 3-6 [10-3]); Hsieh/Ostapenko beat the same #14 seeds 6-4 6-4 on these very courts yesterday. Mihalikova/Nicholls beat Mertens/Shnaider in the Toronto QF; Hsieh/Ostapenko have beaten that pair twice in 2026, including at Cincinnati nine days later. Both chains are hard court, both inside four weeks, both corroborated on two pages. Underneath that, Hsieh/Ostapenko are a nine-month unit with two 2025 slam finals and a 2026 title; Mertens/Shnaider are a North-American-swing pairing playing their first slam together, away from their regular partners, 5-2 lifetime with two pre-USO losses. Fresher (2R walkover) and Mertens is the best doubles player on court, but chemistry and match reps sit with the seeds. I make it ~64%, a modest step above the price.

rows.headline: Lajovic's clay 'specialism' is a 2019 label; his 2026 clay is 5-6 with losses to #180-200
rows.analysis: The price (Kalshi 0.57/0.58, books 1.66 vs 2.06) discounts a #65 to near coin-flip because clay is supposed to be the 36-year-old Serb's surface. It isn't anymore. Lajovic's 2026 clay ledger: 1R loss to Cecchinato at Montemar as the 8 seed, R16 loss to Roca Batalla (#~200) at Cattolica, R16 loss to Rocha at Perugia, RG qualifying 1R loss to Rodionov, Umag 1R loss to Van Assche. His only good 2026 stretch was on HARD (Lexington SF, beat Bonzi in Cincy qualy). He hasn't hit a clay ball in a match since June 12. Landaluce, by contrast, made a Rome QF on clay as a lucky loser beating Cilic, Bellucci and Medjedovic, took Medvedev to 7-5 in the third, and made RG R3 through two five-setters. He beat Lajovic 6-3 6-1 last October and beat Cecchinato on clay a fortnight after Lajovic lost to him. Add a wildcard-into-Davis-Cup-prep motivation edge and warm, quick Seville conditions that suit the 193cm hitter. The counter is genuine: Landaluce is streaky (April clay losses to Quinn and Collignon) and Lajovic still constructs points well on dirt. That caps this at bronze.

rows.headline: Biolay is the better clay player and 279 ranks higher; books have her 62%, Kalshi 50%
rows.analysis: Two French players, no meeting at any level I could find. Biolay (#713, career high, 25) is a 2025 UCF grad on the way up: All-Big 12 first team, college #57, a win over then-#18 Komar, and this February she took a set off Arantxa Rus at Macon. Mattel (#992, 26) is a career ITF-W15 grinder whose singles peak was #950 and whose real strength is doubles (#333). Clay is Biolay's better half by record (42-24 vs Mattel's 22-19) and Dijon is outdoor clay at Lac Kir. At the three events they both entered this summer Biolay went deeper twice (qualified at Macon where Mattel did not; QF at Nogent-sur-Marne where Mattel lost R16), tied at Knokke. The one real point for Mattel is last week: she qualified into the W50 Saint-Palais main draw and won a set off Emma Lene, while Biolay lost the final qualifying round 7-6 5-7 4-6. Books price Biolay 1.55; Kalshi's thin ~$1.7k book has it 50/50. I take Biolay, but neither is in hot form.

rows.title: Onclin vs Perot
rows.tournament: Cassis Open Provence (Challenger 75) R32, outdoor hard, Cassis, France
rows.headline: Onclin beat him 6-0 in the decider in March and owns this surface; 0.63 is light
rows.analysis: Onclin (#158, career high, 6th seed) is simply a level up: two Abidjan Challenger titles, a Tampere SF, and an ATP Stuttgart R16 where he beat Marozsan (#54). On hard he is 29-8 in 2026. Perot (#338) is a clay/M25 grinder — 26-17 on clay, 7-11 in Challenger main draws all year, with no 2026 win over anyone near #250. They met in March on indoor hard at M25 Toulouse-Balma: Onclin won 6-4 3-6 6-0 and took the title. Perot arrives hot — his third summer M25 title Sunday at Bagneres (5 matches in 6 days, 3-set final) — but he was in exactly this spot after Koksijde in August and lost Challenger 1R twice, including to #424 Brunold. The counter is real: Onclin hasn't played since a flat US Open qualifying loss to Sachko (#199) on 25 Aug, has flown back from the North American swing, and has seven Challenger first-round exits in 2026. Transitive chains (Loge, Moeller favour Perot; Ghazouani Durand favours Onclin) cancel. Rust and a home crowd shave it, but not to a coin flip.

rows.title: Schaefer vs Lazarenko
rows.tournament: W15 Viserba di Rimini (Rimini Cup) R32/1R main draw, outdoor clay
rows.headline: Defending Viserba champ, match-tight, vs an 18yo 5½ weeks off after a retirement
rows.analysis: Schaefer's #1018 badly understates her: she plays 2-3 events a year, and the one she plays best is this one — she won W15 Viserba in Sep 2025 from qualifying, 7-0, beating Chiesa (#575, CH #143) in a 3-hour final. In the same draw Lazarenko lost R16 to Sevcikova, whom Schaefer then beat in the QF: a clean same-courts chain, if a year old. Schaefer is also match-tight, having played singles and doubles at Fiano Romano last week; Lazarenko hasn't hit a competitive ball since retiring at 0-4 down on 31 Jul, a 5½-week gap confirmed on tennisexplorer and coretennis. Against that: Lazarenko is 366 spots higher, at career high, 19-11 in 2026 with a W15 final and two SFs, 18 vs 39, and Schaefer's only 2026 evidence is 1-1, the loss coming to Federica Trevisan (CH #1227) who then took the title. That is why this is a lean, not a medal. Venue mastery, rhythm and rust tip it to Schaefer; the market at ~0.55 has most of it already.

rows.title: Torner Sensano vs Cherubini
rows.tournament: W35 Reus Open (Club Tennis Reus Monterols), R1, outdoor clay
rows.headline: Cherubini is a level up and just made a W50 clay QF; Torner is a W15 player
rows.analysis: Torner's 27-11 2026 record is almost entirely W15: Manacor title, Ontinyent and Getxo finals, all against sub-#500 fields. Every time she steps up she loses — Sakellaridi (W35 Pula, Apr), Esquiva Banuls (W40 Horb, Jul), Siskova at this same $30k Reus event in Sep 2025 — and last week she had to qualify for a W15 in Badalona and still lost R1 to Mair 6-4 6-2. Cherubini, #378 and 6th seed, was in the W50 Saint-Palais-sur-Mer quarters on clay four days ago (d. Martynov 6-4 6-1, d. Wolff 7-6(6) 6-1, l. Ferro), and beat Friedsam in July. Her 15-24 season looks awful until you see it is mostly W50/W75/WTA qualifying. Against Torner: the one real transitive chain (Maria Toma, #826) favours Torner, and Cherubini's floor is genuinely low — she lost to Toma as a 1.10 favourite. Home Catalan clay and youth keep this closer than the rank gap suggests, but the better player is Cherubini and ~62% is about right. No independent, unpriced factor here, so no medal.

transitive.summary: Only one usable chain (Toma, #826) and it favours Torner, but both were heavy favourites and it is a low-quality shared opponent. Cherubini's W50 week outranks anything in Torner's ledger.

rows.title: Nguyen Tan vs Granwehr
rows.tournament: Montreux Nestlé Open (WTA 125) R32, outdoor clay, Montreux Tennis Club, Switzerland
rows.headline: Nguyen Tan bagelled Granwehr on clay in June and is the sharper of two slumping players
rows.analysis: Both are mid-300s/400s grinders in patchy form, so the market's 62% on Granwehr looks like a ranking-and-home-wildcard price rather than a read. The most relevant fact is three months old and on this surface: Nguyen Tan beat Granwehr 6-3 6-0 at W75 Blois, and leads the H2H 2-1 (also 6-1 6-4 in the 2024 Madrid W15 final; Granwehr's win was 2023). Nguyen Tan's 2026 clay ceiling is higher — qualified and won a WTA 125 main-draw match at Saint-Malo, SF at W75 Blois — while Granwehr's peak is a W35 Aix title and she has lost 1R at W15 level twice in August. The Bujumbura chain (Nguyen Tan d. Nahimana #231 6-4 6-2; Granwehr lost to her) points the same way. Against that: Granwehr is 113 spots higher, a fresh home wildcard, beat Kabbaj a day after Kabbaj beat Nguyen Tan at Aix, and Nguyen Tan plays a third day running in 28-30C with a doubles draw too. Genuine coin flip with a lean, not a conviction call.

edge_factors.detail: RCB made 2 Challenger finals (Murcia, Cattolica) beating Ofner, de Jong, Kukushkin, Travaglia; Ritschard has 0 Challenger MD wins on clay in 2026

Sept 2024 Sevilla: Ritschard lost SF to Altmaier 6-7(6) 7-6(3) 6-7(4); RCB beat Altmaier in the final 6-3 7-5

rows.headline: Three-time champion of this event; Ritschard's hot streak is all M25 Futures
rows.analysis: Two prices (Kalshi 0.53, book 1.72) both discount Carballes Baena hard for one fact: he retired at 5-7 2-2 vs #538 Vives Marcos in Porto qualifying on Aug 31. That is real and it caps my confidence, but no cause was reported, he is entered eight days later, and his 2026 is littered with hard-court qualifying misfires while his clay level stayed high: Challenger finals at Murcia and Cattolica with wins over Ofner, de Jong, Kukushkin, Travaglia. Ritschard's 11-1 run is entirely M25 Futures (Oviedo title, Santander final) plus Swiss interclub; his only 2026 Challenger clay match was a first-round qualifying loss to Gombos at Zug. He is six months back from a Jan-to-July layoff that dropped him #131 to #638. Slow, heavy Seville clay blunts a 6'4" flat hitter and rewards exactly what RCB does. He is 15-1 here since 2022. Counterweight is honest: Ritschard has two wins on these courts this week, RCB comes in cold at 23-25 and unseeded for the first time in years, and Ritschard was a point from beating Altmaier here in 2024. Bronze, not silver.

Bookmakers price this 1.66/2.06 (~60% implied for Janvier) — the inverse of Kalshi's thin 46-47/53-54 market ($520 vs $2 volume, looks retail not sharp). Janvier leads the H2H 1-0, winning 6-4 6-3 in Mar 2026 (Cherbourg, indoor hard — same surface family as this outdoor-hard R1). Shared opponent Laurent Lokoli (#409) also favors Janvier: he beat Lokoli in three sets in June, while Ghazouani Durand lost to him in the Bastia M25 final in July (both on clay, so it's a surface-mismatched but recent read). Janvier's 2026 losses were all to clearly better, in-form players (Chidekh #205 on a title run, Simakin #275, Kuzmanov #375 twice) — competitive, not routs — while Ghazouani Durand has a bad loss to #1283-ranked Kielan on Aug 30 mixed into his run. Ghazouani Durand does arrive fresher (two straight-sets qualifying wins vs Janvier's gritty 7-5-third win), and both just survived qualifying, so live form cuts slightly his way. No single fact settles it, but four independent, verifiable threads converge on Janvier.

Since mid-April he is roughly 2-8 with retirements at Busan (Apr 16) and Royan (Jun 17), a single event since mid-June, and no match at all since losing to Galan at Bonn on Jul 28 - six weeks cold. Ymer is the 5 seed, ranked 46 spots higher, and has played four matches in three weeks including a US Open qualifying win. His 'clay specialist' label (career 244-167 clay vs 102-117 hard) is stale: his best recent results are hard-court Asian Challengers - Kobe final and Seoul SF in late 2025, Chennai final Feb 2025. The obvious counter is his Sept 1 collapse in Zhangjiagang, but ATP attributed it to nausea plus extreme heat/humidity, and Shanghai on Tuesday is forecast ~26C, ~52% humidity, breezy at 3pm - very different conditions, seven days on. Kotov's ceiling (ex-#50) keeps this near a coin flip, but the live evidence favours Ymer.

The books have Shao at 1.58 (58%) and Kalshi mirrors it, but the bodies of work are lopsided. Nakajima, 15, has played 34 Futures qualifying matches in 2026 and is 10-4 on Chinese hard since Aug 2, reaching the final qualifying round in four of five weeks and qualifying once (Tianjin). Shao, 18, has played SEVEN matches in all of 2026: a J100 Chengdu QF, one M15 attempt that ended 3-6 and a retirement, and this week's two wins over an unranked 19-year-old junior and an unranked 27-year-old doubles player. His 2025 base was J30 finals and J60 semis - the bottom junior tiers. The one direct link is Markosian: Nakajima beat him 6-4 6-2; Shao was down a set to him and pulled out - and Markosian is 2-8 on the year, bagelled 6-0 6-2 by a man Nakajima beat. Shao is bigger and at home, which is why the price sits where it does, but nothing in his record says he can hold a men's baseline.

rows.title: Borisiouk vs Matsuda
rows.tournament: Sport Festival Challenger Phan Thiet (Challenger 50, Vietnam) R32, outdoor hard
rows.headline: Matsuda is the better player at this level and owns the live Singh chain; price is a coin flip
rows.analysis: First-round Challenger 50 match on outdoor hard in Phan Thiet, third on Court C Tuesday (court starts 10:00 local, so roughly 07:00-08:00 UTC). Books have it 1.82/1.83, a pure coin flip. Rankings are far apart: Matsuda #483 (CH 451) is a Challenger regular who qualified and won a main-draw match in Zhangjiagang last week (beat Delaney #365 in two tiebreaks) before losing 3-6 2-6 to Leong; Borisiouk #1003 (CH 736) is a Futures grinder playing up, though he is 16-3 in 2026 with an M15 Wuning title and just beat #548 Kumasaka 6-4 6-2 and #1265 Cook 6-3 6-2 in qualifying here. The one live shared opponent, Karan Singh (#604, right-handed 188cm), favours Matsuda: Matsuda beat him 6-4 6-4 at Samsun in July while Borisiouk lost to him in three at Astana two weeks later, both on hard. Against that, Borisiouk is 191cm, grooved on these courts, and Matsuda's margins are paper-thin: his last four wins were all tiebreak or third-set squeakers and his losses (Leong, Matsuoka, Ho, Brouwer) were lopsided, suggesting a counterpuncher who gets overpowered by bigger hitters. Net: a modest Matsuda lean on level and the Singh chain, no medal because the market already prices near 50/50 and the counter-case is real.

rows.title: Kulikova vs Kaji
rows.tournament: ITF W50 Guiyang (China) R32, outdoor hard, ~1,100m altitude
rows.headline: Lefty power vs a retriever who loses to power; but Kulikova retired 5 days ago, cause unknown
rows.analysis: W50 Guiyang first round, outdoor hard at ~1,100m, first match Tuesday (10:00 local, 02:00 UTC; Kalshi's 08:00 UTC is a placeholder). Books have it a coin flip (Kulikova 1.87, Kaji 1.81). Kaji (#259, 31yo) is a right-handed grinder who beats Japanese/Asian journeywomen and gets flattened by anyone with pace: 2026 losses to Costoulas 6-1 6-0, Preston 6-3 6-1 and 6-0 6-2, Monnot 6-2 6-0, Stefanini 6-3 6-1, Encheva 6-2 6-2, plus three straight R16 exits in the last three weeks. Kulikova (#310, ex-#179, 1.77m lefty) has the higher ceiling: W75 Lexington title in August beating Akli, Collins, Broadus, and last week beat Yao Xinxin 6-4 6-2, a player Kaji is 0-2 against. She also won their only meeting, 7-5 7-5 on hard at Nonthaburi Jan 2023. Altitude makes the ball fly and favours the hitter over the retriever. The problem: Kulikova RETIRED trailing Garland 6-1 3-2 on Sept 3 and no source explains why; that either signals a real physical issue (Kaji's grind then wins) or a tactical bail while losing to a #200 player before travelling to Guiyang. She is on the order of play, so she intends to play. Lean Kulikova at 55% on the style and transitive reads, but the unexplained retirement keeps confidence too low for a medal.

Xia (19, CHN, ATP #2282, career high #2170) is a Q-R16 regular who qualified and won a main-draw match at this venue in May and went 6-0 6-1, 6-0 6-2 this week. Dorokhov (18, RUS, no ATP ranking) lost three straight Q-1Rs at Monastir in May-June, then in China beat only Q-1R-level players (Lan, Pan, a retirement vs Lu) and lost to Yamamoto, Osminkin (#2245) and Guo Cuihaozhe (6-11 this year) at this same Wuning venue last week. The chains are recent, same surface and same venue: Guo, who beat Dorokhov, was crushed 6-1 6-1 by Jones and 6-3 6-3 by Yang, the two players who beat Xia only narrowly. Two direct shared opponents (Xie Xinyuan, Lan Jintao) show Xia winning comfortably where Dorokhov scraped or won modestly. Xia's weakness is that he loses Q-R16s often (5-6 in 2026), but those losses came to players ranked 1500-2000, a tier above Dorokhov. Bookmakers 1.66/2.05 (about 57%); I make it closer to 64%. The match-tiebreak third set in ITF qualifying keeps variance high, which caps conviction at bronze.

rows.headline: Ochi is grooved at Sapporo and owns the Samrej chain; Mochizuki arrives 0-4 and cold
rows.analysis: Kalshi's date is a placeholder: this is a first-round match at the ITF M25 Sapporo on outdoor hard, listed by tennisexplorer/betexplorer for Sept 8 around 02:00 UTC (11:00 local); the ITF order of play was not reachable, so treat the hour as approximate. The ranking gap (Mochizuki #664 vs Ochi #1146) overstates the difference: Ochi is a 30-year-old lefty, ex-#343, 29-20 in 2026 (19-12 hard) mostly at M15/M25 level, while Mochizuki is 16-23 this year. Mochizuki won an M15 title in Tianjin (Aug 4-9, weak field) but has since lost four straight main-draw matches in straight sets, including to #1143 Koyama and #1027 Meng, and has not played since Aug 26. Ochi qualified here for a second straight week, beating Nakanishi (#2003) 6-4 6-2 today after a 6-0 6-0, and last week reached the R16 before losing 3-6 6-4 6-7(2) to #616 Lee Kuan-Yi as a 2.31 dog. The one live chain is strong and same-surface: Ochi beat Samrej (#486, just a Challenger finalist) twice this year while Samrej beat Mochizuki two weeks ago. Against that, Mochizuki leads the H2H 2-0 on hard (Ochi retired in 2019; 6-4 6-2 at Lexington 2023 qualifying), knows Ochi's lefty game intimately as his regular doubles partner, and has the higher ceiling. Bookmakers price Mochizuki around 1.65 to Ochi 2.10. I make it a genuine coin flip with the feather on Ochi for current form and rhythm, but nowhere near a medal bar.

Lee (#143, 24, Georgia Tech grad, 77-20 in 2025) is on the best run of her career: Warsaw 125 title in August beating top seed Jacquemot (#62), Knutson and Valdmannova, then a competitive 6-4 6-7 6-4 loss to P. Style fit favours Lee: a taller, bigger server with baseline discipline against a teenager whose serve is the soft spot. Bookmakers (1.60-1.74 Lee) sit around 58-60%; I make Lee about 63%.

rows.title: Bax vs Jones

rows.headline: Bax is the better 2026 player, but his Sept 5 retirement caps the conviction
rows.analysis: Phan Thiet 3 is a $63k hard-court Challenger; ATP's daily schedule has Bax (4th seed) vs Jones first on Court C at 10:00 local Tuesday, i.e. 03:00 UTC, not Kalshi's 06:00. Bookmakers price Bax 1.64-1.79 (about 58%) against Jones 1.92-2.10; Kalshi at 53-54c is cheaper than the books. Bax (#303, CH 247 in July) is 36-23 in 2026, roughly 19-12 on hard, reached the Brazzaville Challenger final and won hard-court matches at Nonthaburi and Phan Thiet in January in these exact conditions. Jones (#489, CH 301) has fallen apart in 2026: since February he has beaten only Sun, Jasika, Matsuoka, Rawat and Vales at Challenger level, lost to Sekulic and Martin Tiffon twice each, dropped M15 matches in Tokyo, withdrew from Pozoblanco in July with a reported left knee problem, sat out seven weeks, then on return won two Mallorca qualifying matches before losing 0-6 4-6 to 17-year-old #530 Ivan Ivanov. Jones owns the H2H (Abidjan 2025, 6-7(5) 6-4 6-4) but that was during his title week 17 months ago. The real counter is Bax himself: he retired trailing 6-7(7) 3-4 to Bouzige in the M15 Nonthaburi semifinal on Sept 5, three days before this match, with no public explanation. If the retirement was body-preservation ahead of a seeded Challenger week, Bax should win; if it is a live injury, the price is a trap. That unresolved question keeps this at a lean, not a medal.

rows.title: Osaka vs Rybakina
rows.tournament: US Open R4 (round of 16), outdoor hard, Louis Armstrong Stadium
rows.headline: Rybakina is the better hard-court player and beat Osaka a month ago, but both are hurt
rows.analysis: US Open R4 on Armstrong, not before 2:30pm ET Monday. Rybakina (#2, 42-13, AO champion, IW and Toronto finalist) beat Osaka (#13) 4-6 7-6(5) 6-4 in Toronto four weeks ago in the same conditions, but had to save four break points at 3-2 in the third and made 72 unforced errors, so Osaka's flat, early-taken ball clearly troubles her. Osaka is 0-2 against top-10 players on hard courts this year (1-7 overall, the only win on grass at Wimbledon) and has laboured through this draw: two tiebreaks without a break of serve vs #102 Zakharova, three sets vs #39 Siniakova, then 2h38 vs #20 Mertens with a medical timeout on her chronic left Achilles at 3-4 in the decider ('shocked I won'). Rybakina has not dropped a set (6-3 6-2, 6-2 6-4, 7-6(6) 6-3) though she was broken at 4-4 and saved a set point vs #74 Starodubtseva, and her left heel tendon (retired Cincinnati QF Aug 21, seven days off, mixed doubles withdrawn) is felt most on the serve landing. Hard-court chains lean Rybakina: same-week Miami she beat Gibson 6-2 6-2 while Osaka lost to her; Rybakina went 1-2 in tight matches with Sabalenka while Osaka lost 2-6 4-6 at IW. Two wins from World No.1 is a real carrot. Both are compromised, so this stays near a coin flip: Rybakina about 59%, no medal.
